title: The coat, unwashed
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Tuesday. The owner says the coat could stand a wash. Wood says it's the same coat. She says that's not an answer. He says if you wash it it's a different coat. She says that's not how coats work. He says it's how this one works.

panels.composition: The shop. The OWNER at her station, glancing at WOOD's coat, its cuff, its stain. Wood at the cutter.

image.prompt: a woman in reading glasses glancing at a young man's stained and frayed chore coat as he works at a mat cutter, black and white, no words

balloons.text: Wash it and it's a different coat.

image.prompt: a woman in reading glasses, dry, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The stain. The cuff. The button. Three things. Kept.

image.prompt: close on a canvas coat's ink stain, frayed cuff and mismatched button, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The owner going back to work. Not pressing it. The coat stays. It's how this one works; she's decided to let it. The strip: fifteen strokes.

image.prompt: a woman in reading glasses returning to her work while a young man in a chore coat cuts a mat, drawn in fifteen sparse strokes, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen over rough blue pencil; xerox grain; stark spotting; rain in frantic vertical hatching (Arc 1's aesthetic)

notes: 'It's how this one works.' Unwashed till 2011.
